clue.text: To supervise a lab possibly requires procedure around computers, etc (3-3)

indicators.note: something turned around faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: a step is a procedure; turned around it reads PETS
IT = information technology

annotation.surface: A job ad for someone to run a science laboratory, with a nod to its computer procedures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lab' looks like a laboratory, but it is a Labrador dog, which is why the definition carries 'possibly'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: minding a Labrador while its owners are away is one kind of animal-minding job.

clue.text: Cockney restoring part of their city (6)

indicators.note: London Cockney speech famously drops the H at the start of a word

blocks.note: restoring = HEALING; a Cockney says it without the H

annotation.surface: A Cockney doing up a corner of London.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockneys are Londoners, so 'their city' is London; the definition only makes sense once the Cockney is read.
annotation.definitionFit: A west London borough, so a district of the Cockneys' own city.

clue.text: Abandoned garage isn’t a place soldiers may gather (7,4)

indicators.note: abandoned behaviour is wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A disused garage is judged unsuitable as a muster point for troops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as deserted, but here it means unrestrained.
annotation.definitionFit: A military term for the assembly point where troops and kit gather before an operation.

clue.text: Have hospital completely housed in extremely tasteless civic buildings (4,5)

indicators.note: a thing housed in another lives inside it, so the middle pieces sit within the outer letters
the extremes of a word are its two ends, first and last letters

blocks.note: to have = to own
H = hospital, as on road signs
all = completely
the ends of TASTELESS, wrapped around OWN H ALL

annotation.surface: A complaint that a hospital has been put entirely into ugly municipal buildings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tasteless' sounds like a verdict on the architecture; only its two ends are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the seats of local government in each town are its civic buildings.

clue.text: Tie is boring and the opposite of cool? (4,4)

blocks.note: a dead evening is a boring one
cool against heat

annotation.surface: Someone decides a necktie is both dull and uncool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tie' is a result, not a necktie.
annotation.definitionFit: A sporting term: a race where two runners cross the line together ends level.

clue.text: Alternately, dirty, intense, and ultimately hilarious feature of some humour (7)

indicators.note: alternately means by turns, one on and one off, so every other letter is kept
ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: D-R-Y from dIrTy, first, third and fifth letters
iNtEnSe alternately, second, fourth and sixth letters
the last letter of hilariouS

annotation.surface: A description of comedy that is rude, full-on and funny in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alternately' works on both dirty and intense, picking odd letters from one and even from the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A deadpan, understated manner is prized in British comedy, so it is one feature some humour has.

clue.text: Make sense of publicity trick, mostly (3,2)

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: an ad is publicity
DUPE (trick) without its final E

annotation.surface: Trying to see through a publicity stunt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make sense of' looks like the definition, but the definition is 'Make sense' and 'of' just joins it on.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a story that is coherent, whose figures total correctly, is said to be convincing in this phrase.

clue.text: Fashionable joint (3)

blocks.note: a slang word for trendy
the ball-and-socket joint at the top of the leg

annotation.surface: A trendy bar or club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint' reads as a venue, but it is the body part.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a slang word for trendy, and the ball-and-socket joint where leg meets pelvis.

clue.text: Fancy crest adopted by one unspecified family (8)

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate, dressed up, so the letters are rearranged
a child adopted by a family is taken in, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: any = one, no matter which
CREST rearranged, sitting between AN and Y

annotation.surface: An elaborate coat of arms is taken up by some anonymous family.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crest' and 'family' paint heraldry, which is fitting for the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one's line of descent, the family one comes from.

clue.text: Distinct width always once needed for restricted stretch of road (8)

blocks.note: distinct = clear
W = width
ay (or aye) is an old word for always

annotation.surface: A road-planning note about the width needed for a restricted section.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic word.
annotation.definitionFit: A British road term: a main road on which stopping or parking is banned, hence restricted.

clue.text: Odd bits of data about very long show (6)

indicators.note: the odd-numbered bits, first, third and so on
about means around, so these letters surround what follows

blocks.note: D and T, the first and third letters of DATA
an epic is very long; it sits inside D...T

annotation.surface: Scraps of data about a marathon television programme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like the long programme itself, but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to portray something in a picture or words.

clue.text: A crony of popular comedian Henry (2,4)

definitions.note: the answer is a phrase meaning friendly with someone; 'a crony of' names the same relationship

blocks.note: in = popular, fashionable
a wit is a comic
H = henry, the unit of inductance

annotation.surface: Someone is a pal of a well-loved comic called Henry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like the comedian's name, but it is the physics unit, symbol H.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be on close, favoured terms with someone, as a crony is.

clue.text: Strong drink that in Spain is full of iron (8)

indicators.note: a thing full of something holds it inside, so ESO wraps round the next piece

blocks.note: eso is Spanish for that
to iron clothes is to press them; it goes inside ES...O

annotation.surface: A Spanish drink loaded with iron, like a tonic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strong drink' suggests spirits, but it is coffee.
annotation.definitionFit: A short, concentrated black coffee, strong by design.

clue.text: Improvement seen by re-working the middle of Dennis the Menace (11)

indicators.note: working the material over again gives it a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the central part of a word, here its two middle letters

blocks.note: the two central letters of DENNIS
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A comic-strip artist improves on the Beano's Dennis the Menace.
annotation.walkthrough: Dennis the Menace is a naughty boy in the British comic The Beano; the clue splits his name, taking only the middle of Dennis.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an upgrade that makes something better.

clue.text: Gormley principally does this reshaping work with metal (12)

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so the word gives its first letter
reshaping gives the letters a new form, rearranging them

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the first letter of DOES
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Antony Gormley, the sculptor, mainly makes his art by shaping metal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Principally' looks as if it takes the G of Gormley, but it acts on 'does'; Gormley goes in whole. Antony Gormley is a British sculptor famed for metal figures such as the Angel of the North.
annotation.definitionFit: The craft of working gold, a precious metal, into jewellery and plate.

clue.text: Name nearly added to short film I like (9)

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
a piece added to another is tacked on after it

blocks.note: an ident is a brief film a TV channel shows to identify itself
I as written
CALL (to name) without its last letter

annotation.surface: Naming a short film you enjoy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as a verb of enjoying, but it is the adjective meaning the same as.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the same as, exactly alike.

clue.text: Endless force involved in substantial counter-attack (8)

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter goes
a thing involved in another is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: real = substantial, having substance
PRISE (to force open) without its end; it goes inside RE...AL

annotation.surface: A military report of a big counter-strike using all available force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Force' is a verb here, as in forcing a lid, not an army.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an act of retaliation against an enemy's attack.

clue.text: New money from abroad to encourage theatre operator? (12)

blocks.note: N = new
euros are foreign currency to a Briton
to urge on is to encourage

annotation.surface: Foreign funding arrives to support a stage producer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a stage, but it is an operating theatre; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a brain surgeon works in an operating theatre, so is literally one who operates there.

clue.text: Let back in to study somewhere in Cambridge (7)

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

annotation.surface: A student is allowed back to study at Cambridge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge' points to the English university, but it is the Cambridge in Massachusetts.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to allow entry again, to a hospital, a club or a college.

clue.text: Lower limits of difference, on average (6)

indicators.note: the limits of a thing are its boundaries, so the first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of DIFFERENCE
the mean is an average

annotation.surface: A statistics note on the lower bounds of a difference from the mean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as an adjective in a statistics sentence, but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to degrade or cheapen someone's dignity, as in 'lower oneself'.

clue.text: Elite players failing to finish meal (5,3)

indicators.note: a word that fails to finish stops short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: the cream is the elite, the best
TEAM without its last letter

annotation.surface: A top sports team loses a match it could not close out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'finish' about a match; it is only about the word TEAM.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a British afternoon spread of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.

clue.text: Pegs securing the bottom of particular boxes? (5)

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, here inside
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: tees are pegs a golfer sets a ball on
the last letter of PARTICULAR, held inside TE...ES

annotation.surface: Tent pegs hold down the base of some crates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' look like containers, but box is a kind of evergreen shrub; the question mark marks the example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: box is an evergreen shrub or small tree used for hedging.

clue.text: Ancient city not quite superior to all others (6)

indicators.note: not quite means just short of complete, so the last letter goes

blocks.clueFragment: not quite superior to all others
blocks.note: THE BEST without its last letter

annotation.surface: An old city that almost beat all its rivals.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase must be read as three words, THE BEST, before it is trimmed.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the name belongs both to a capital of ancient Egypt and to a city of ancient Greece.

clue.text: What may be left behind back of store, say (6)

blocks.note: the last letter of STORE
to say = to state

annotation.surface: Something forgotten at the back of a shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left behind' suggests a forgotten item, but it means left after death.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: the property and money a person leaves when they die.

clue.text: Donkey jacket belonging to aimless son (3)

indicators.note: a jacket is the outer layer, so the word gives its first and last letters

blocks.note: the outer letters of AIMLESS
S = son

annotation.surface: A donkey jacket owned by a directionless young man.
annotation.walkthrough: A donkey jacket is a heavy British work coat; the clue splits the phrase so 'Donkey' is the definition and 'jacket' an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the older word for the same long-eared beast of burden.

clue.text: Overturned river barge contains head of rotting fish (8)

indicators.note: a boat overturned is upside down, so the word runs backwards
the barge holds the next letter inside it
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the Cam, Cambridge's river, turned back to front
a keel is a flat-bottomed coal barge, especially on the Tyne
the first letter of ROTTING, inside KE...EL

annotation.surface: A capsized river barge holds a rotting fish head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' belongs with the river, not the barge. The River Cam flows through Cambridge.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a striped, oily sea fish common around British coasts.

clue.text: Compact cupboard holding second-hand equipment primarily (5-3)

indicators.note: the cupboard holds the next letters inside it
primarily means in the first place, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.note: a closet is a cupboard
the first letters of SECOND-HAND and EQUIPMENT, inside CLOSE...T

annotation.surface: A small cupboard full of used gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compact' sounds like describing the small cupboard, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: placed near together, as eyes or teeth can be.

clue.text: Cuban female maybe retiring in Milan, Italy (6)

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the letters read backwards
the answer lies in the words that follow

blocks.note: milAN ITALy, read backwards

annotation.surface: A Cuban woman is staying quietly in Milan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests someone shy or taking retirement in Italy; here it sends the letters backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a woman from Cuba is one of Latin American heritage, hence the 'maybe'.
